claims.evidence: MedlinePlus valacyclovir: antiviral for cold sores, chickenpox, shingles, genital herpes; NHS aciclovir uses likewise.
claims.newSentence: Antiviral medicines used for herpes virus infections such as cold sores, shingles, chickenpox and genital herpes. Aciclovir is described on this site, and valaciclovir is a related medicine.

claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: synthetic nucleoside analogue; stops spread of herpes virus.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus describes aciclovir as a synthetic nucleoside analogue antiviral that works by stopping the spread of the herpes virus in the body.

claims.evidence: NHS: stops the herpes virus growing and spreading and helps the immune system.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says aciclovir stops the herpes virus growing and spreading, which helps the immune system deal with the infection.

claims.evidence: LiverTox: valacyclovir is a nucleoside analogue antiviral and prodrug of acyclovir.
claims.newSentence: NIH LiverTox describes valaciclovir as a nucleoside analogue antiviral and a prodrug of aciclovir.

claims.evidence: NHS: no medicine removes the herpes virus completely.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says no medicine or treatment removes the herpes virus from the body completely.

claims.evidence: emc SmPC: allergy to aciclovir or valaciclovir.
claims.newSentence: UK product information lists allergy to aciclovir or valaciclovir as a reason the medicine is not used.

claims.evidence: emc SmPC: renal elimination; dosage adjustment in renal impairment.
claims.newSentence: UK product information says aciclovir is cleared through the kidneys, so treatment may be adjusted in kidney problems.

claims.evidence: emc SmPC: probenecid and cimetidine increase aciclovir exposure.
emc SmPC: aciclovir raises theophylline exposure.
First pass listed mycophenolate mofetil and aminophylline as NHS-named interacting medicines; not seen in retrieved text.
NHS: serious allergic reaction 999; liver/kidney/blood effects 111.
First pass: 'A serious allergic reaction is rare' - 'rare' not in retrieved text.
First pass urlAliases 'nucleoside-analogue-antivirals' and 'antiherpes-antivirals' were invented search names; no source uses them as class names.

notes: Doubts: valaciclovir is a member name with no page on the site (compiler should be run to confirm that members need not be pages); urlAliases emptied; the class concept 'nucleoside antiviral' for valaciclovir rests on LiverTox, not MedlinePlus (MedlinePlus labels it only 'antiviral').
